subQuestions.subQuestion: Explain the purpose of using KHCO<sub>3</sub> in bread baking.
subQuestions.subAnswer: CO<sub>2</sub> gas produced makes the bread rise / spongy / soft.

subQuestions.subQuestion: Write the chemical equation for the decomposition of KHCO<sub>3</sub> upon heating.
subQuestions.subAnswer:
2KHCO<sub>3</sub> → K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub> 
(Accept fraction)

subQuestions.subQuestion:
The enthalpy change of decomposition of KHCO<sub>3</sub>(s) can be determined indirectly from the enthalpy changes of the following two reactions:

KHCO<sub>3</sub>(s) + HCl(aq) →KCl(aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O(l) + CO<sub>2</sub> ------ Reaction (1)

K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>(s) + 2HCl(aq) → 2KCl(aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O(l) + CO<sub>2</sub>(g) ------ Reaction (2)

In an experiment to determine the enthalpy change of Reaction (1), 3.39 g of KHCO<sub>3</sub>(s) was added to excess HCl(aq) in an expanded polystyrene cup. The experimental data obtained are shown below:


![](images/Topic8/dse2012-8-1778655459044-inline-subq-text-subqimg-1778654757364-6882-mp3pjgcz-4605.png)
Assuming that the heat capacity of the cup used is negligible, calculate the enthaply change of Reaction (1) from the above data.

In another experiment performed under the same conditions, the enthaply change of Reaction (2) was found to be -49.1 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate the enthalpy change of decomposition of KHCO<sub>3</sub>(s) under the experimental conditions.
subQuestions.subAnswer:
ΔH = 19.6 - (-49.1 x 0.5) / 0.5(+19.6 x 2) - (-49.1)) = +44.15 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>
(Accept +44.1 to +44.2 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>) (the unit must be correct)

The following experiment was carried out to determine the enthalpy change of solution of ammonium nitrate:

![](images/Topic8/dse2013-5-1778781808492-inline-q-qimg-1778781204002-9173-mp5srjpz-5350.png)

A certain volume of water was placed in an expanded polystyrene cup. The temperature of the water in the cup was measured with a thermometer at half-minute intervals. Right at the third minute, 2.0 g of NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub>(s) was added to the cup. The solution in the cup was then stirred thoroughly and its temperature was measured for an additional 7 minutes.

The recordings of temperature are shown in the graph below:

![](images/Topic8/dse2013-5-1778781808492-inline-q-qimg-1778781283038-851-mp5srlbt-9724.png)

subQuestions.subQuestion: ![](images/Topic8/dse2013-5-1778781808492-inline-subq-text-subqimg-1778781323422-8072-mp5srnfb-4549.png)
From the graph, estimate the greatest temperature drop of the solution in the cup.

The mass of the NH<sub>4</sub>OH<sub>3</sub>(aq) obtained was found to be 21.8 g. Calculate the enthalpy change of solution of ammonium nitrate, in kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>, under the experimental conditions.
(Assume that the heat capacity of the expanded polystyrene cup is negligible, and the specific heat capacity of the NH<sub>4</sub>OH<sub>3</sub>(aq) obtained is 4.3 J g<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>.)
subQuestions.subAnswer:
Heat absorbed = mcΔT = 21.8 x 4.3 x 6.8 = 637.4 J
No. of moles of NH<sub>4</sub>OH<sub>3</sub>(s) used = 2.0 / 80 = 0.025
ΔH = +(637.4 / 0.025) = +25.5 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>

subQuestions.subQuestion: Suggest ONE way of keeping NH<sub>4</sub>OH<sub>3</sub>(s) dry during storage.
subQuestions.subAnswer: Place NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub>(s) in a desiccator / sealed container containing drying agent (anhydrous CaCl<sub>2</sub>, CaO(s), MgSO<sub>4</sub>, etc.) / silica gel.

topics: Topic 5: Fossil fuels and Carbon Compounds
questions.question: Petrol is a commonly used motor car fuel. It can be obtained from petroleum by fractional distillation.

subQuestions.subQuestion: Explain, from molecular level, why petrol can be obtained from petroleum by fractional distillation.
subQuestions.subAnswer:
Components having different boiling points can be separated from each other by fractional distillation.
The longer the carbon chain, the higher its boiling point.

subQuestions.subQuestion: Other than directly obtaining petrol from fractional distillation of petroleum, suggest a way for producing extra petrol.
subQuestions.subAnswer: Cracking of heavy oil/heavy hydrocarbon fractions

subQuestions.subQuestion: Octane (C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub>) is a component of petrol. Using octane as an example, state the meaning of the term ‘standard enthalpy change of combustion’ with the aid of a chemical equation.
subQuestions.subAnswer:
The enthalpy change when one molecule of a compound (/ substance / octane) burns completely under standard conditions/25°C and 1 atm.

C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub>(l) + 25/2 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 8CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 9H<sub>2</sub>O(l)
(The eq. should have correct state symbols)

subQuestions.subQuestion: Motor cars powered by petrol emit air pollutants such as nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide. Installing a certain device in motor cars can convert these two oxides to less harmful substances.
Name this device.
subQuestions.subAnswer: Catalytic converter

subQuestions.subAnswer:
ΔH<sup>o</sup> = 2(-394) - 2(-110.5) - 2(90.3)

questions.question: Natural gas is an important energy source for electricity generation. It contains mainly methane (CH<sub>4</sub>).

subQuestions.subQuestion: Write the general formula of the molecules in the homologous series that methane belongs to.
subQuestions.subAnswer: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>

subQuestions.subQuestion:
The combustion of methane is an exothermic reaction. Its chemical equation is shown below:

CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

Complete the table below by stating all the covalent bond(s) that are broken and formed during the combustion of methane.

![](images/Topic8/dse2015-8-1778859559009-inline-subsubq-text-subsubqimg-1778859448801-1505-mp7325ct-5111.png)
Suggest why the combustion is exothermic in terms of the breaking and forming of covalent bonds.
subQuestions.subAnswer: The total energy released in the bond forming process is larger than the total energy absorbed in the bond breaking process.

subQuestions.subQuestion:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change of combustion of methane.
(Standard enthalpy changes of formation:
CH<sub>4</sub>(g) = -74.8 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>; CO<sub>2</sub>(g) = -393.5 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>; H<sub>2</sub>O(l) = -285.9 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>)
subQuestions.subAnswer:
ΔH<sub>c</sub><sup>o</sup> = ΔH<sub>f</sub><sup>o</sup> [CO<sub>2</sub>(g)] + 2ΔH<sub>f</sub><sup>o</sup> [H<sub>2</sub>O(l)] - ΔH<sub>f</sub><sup>o</sup> [CH<sub>4</sub>(g)]
= (-393.5) + 2(-285.9) - (-74.8)
= -890.5 (kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>)

subQuestions.subQuestion: Some regions tend to generate electricity more by natural gas but less by coal. Give TWO reasons from environmental protection consideration.
subQuestions.subAnswer:
Natural gas burns more completely but coal does not. / Burning coal would produce soot / carbon monoxide but burning natural gas would not.
Compared with natural gas, coal contains more impurities. / Burning coal would produce more pollutants, such as SO<sub>2</sub>, metal compound dust.
